{
  "returncode": 0,
  "output_head": "# Fizzy

Guidance for AI coding agents working with this repository.

Fizzy is a kanban-style project management and issue tracker: cards move across columns on boards, with comments, mentions, and assignments.

## Deploy

Default branch: `main`

Self-hosted deploys run Kamal against `config/deploy.yml` — see `docs/kamal-deployment.md`.

## SaaS mode

For local agent work, `tmp/saas.txt` is the checkout-level SaaS switch used by `bin/setup`. When present, read `saas/AGENTS.md` before continuing. Otherwise, do not apply its instructions.

## Architecture Overview

### Multi-Tenancy (URL-Based)

Fizzy uses **URL path-based multi-tenancy**:
- Accounts have a unique decimal `external_account_id` used in URL prefixes
- URLs are prefixed: `/{account_id}/boards/...`
- Middleware (`AccountSlug::Extractor`) extracts the account ID from the URL and sets `Current.account`
- The slug is moved from `PATH_INFO` to `SCRIPT_NAME`, making Rails think it's "mounted" at that path
- Tenant-scoped domain records are account-isolated; global identity, session, and authentication records are exceptions
- Background jobs automatically serialize and restore account context

**Key insight**: This architecture allows multi-tenancy without subdomains or separate databases, making local development and testing simpler.

### Authentication & Authorization

Passwordless magic link authentication. A global `Identity` (email-based) can have `Users` in multiple Accounts, so an email is not a single account membership. Users have roles: owner, admin, member, system. Board-level access control via `Access` records.

### Entropy System

Cards automatically "postpone" (move to "not now") after inactivity:
- Account-level default entropy period
- Board-level entropy override
- Prevents endless todo lists from accumulating
- Configurable via Account/Board settings

### UUID Primary Keys

All tables use UUIDs (UUIDv7 format, base36-encoded as 25-char strings):
- Custom fixture UUID generation maintains deterministic ordering for tests
- Fixtures are always "older" than runtime records
- `.first`/`.last` work correctly in tests

### Background Jobs (Solid Queue)

Database-backed job queue (no Redis):
- Custom `FizzyActiveJobExtensions` prepended to ActiveJob
- Jobs automatically capture/restore `Current.account`
- Mission Control::Jobs for monitoring

Recurring tasks are declared in `config/recurring.yml`.

### Sharded Full-Text Search

Full-text search runs in the database, not Elasticsearch. On MySQL it is sharded 16 ways by CRC32 of the account ID (`Search::Record::Trilogy`); on SQLite it is a single FTS5 index (`Search::Record::SQLite`). Don't assume the sharded shape when working under SQLite. Models in `app/models/search/`.

### Imports and exports

Allow people to move between OSS and SAAS Fizzy instances:
- Exports/Imports can be written to/read from local or S3 storage depending on the config of the instance (both must be supported)
- Must be able to handle very large ZIP files (500+GB)
- Models in `app/models/account/data_transfer/`, `app/models/zip_file`

## Coding style

Before editing or reviewing code, read STYLE.md.
=== STYLE.md ===

# Style

We aim to write code that is a pleasure to read, and we have a lot of opinions about how to do it well. Writing great code is an essential part of our programming culture, and we deliberately set a high bar for every code change anyone contributes. We care about how code reads, how code looks, and how code makes you feel when you read it.

We love discussing code. If you have questions about how to write something, or if you detect some smell you are not quite sure how to solve, please ask away to other programmers. A Pull Request is a great way to do this.

When writing new code, unless you are very familiar with our approach, try to find similar code elsewhere to look for inspiration.

## Conditional returns

In general, we prefer to use expanded conditionals over guard clauses.

```ruby
# Bad
def todos_for_new_group
  ids = params.require(:todolist)[:todo_ids]
  return [] unless ids
  @bucket.recordings.todos.find(ids.split(","))
end

# Good
def todos_for_new_group
  if ids = params.require(:todolist)[:todo_ids]
    @bucket.recordings.todos.find(ids.split(","))
  else
    []
  end
end
```

This is because guard clauses can be hard to read, especially when they are nested.

As an exception, we sometimes use guard clauses to return early from a method:

* When the return is right at the beginning of the method.
* When the main method body is not trivial and involves several lines of code.

```ruby
def after_recorded_as_commit(recording)
  return if recording.parent.was_created?

  if recording.was_created?
    broadcast_new_column(recording)
  else
    broadcast_column_change(recording)
  end
end
```

## Methods ordering

We order methods in classes in the following order:

1. `class` methods
2. `public` methods with `initialize` at the top.
3. `private` methods

## Invocation order

We order m",
  "output_tail": "iers, and we indent the content under them.

```ruby
class SomeClass
  def some_method
    # ...
  end

  private
    def some_private_method_1
      # ...
    end

    def some_private_method_2
      # ...
    end
end
```

If a module only has private methods, we mark it `private` at the top and add an extra new line after but don't indent.

```ruby
module SomeModule
  private
  
  def some_private_method
    # ...
  end
end
```

## CRUD controllers

We model web endpoints as CRUD operations on resources (REST). When an action doesn't map cleanly to a standard CRUD verb, we introduce a new resource rather than adding custom actions.

```ruby
# Bad
resources :cards do
  post :close
  post :reopen
end

# Good
resources :cards do
  resource :closure
end
```

## Controller and model interactions

In general, we favor a [vanilla Rails](https://dev.37signals.com/vanilla-rails-is-plenty/) approach with thin controllers directly invoking a rich domain model. We don't use services or other artifacts to connect the two.

Invoking plain Active Record operations is totally fine:

```ruby
class Cards::CommentsController < ApplicationController
  def create
    @comment = @card.comments.create!(comment_params)
  end
end
```

For more complex behavior, we prefer clear, intention-revealing model APIs that controllers call directly:

```ruby
class Cards::GoldnessesController < ApplicationController
  def create
    @card.gild
  end
end
```

When justified, it is fine to use services or form objects, but don't treat those as special artifacts:

```ruby
Signup.new(email_address: email_address).create_identity
```

## Run async operations in jobs

As a general rule, we write shallow job classes that delegate the logic itself to domain models:

* We typically use the suffix `_later` to flag methods that enqueue a job.
* A common scenario is having a model class that enqueues a job that, when executed, invokes some method in that same class. In this case, we use the suffix `_now` for the regular synchronous method.

```ruby
module Event::Relaying
  extend ActiveSupport::Concern

  included do
    after_create_commit :relay_later
  end

  def relay_later
    Event::RelayJob.perform_later(self)
  end

  def relay_now
    # ...
  end
end

class Event::RelayJob < ApplicationJob
  def perform(event)
    event.relay_now
  end
end
```

steps.reasoning_content:
Here's my analysis of that list, focusing on how I'd approach it given my expertise:

**Diving Deep into Event and Card Rendering Logic**

Alright, let's break this down. My initial thought is to comprehensively understand the event display system. I need to get a handle on all the different rendering components and how they fit together. I see a mix of partials, layouts, and potentially full-page views. This suggests a modular design, which is good, but I need to map the whole flow.

First, I'm going to focus on the core event representation. I'll meticulously read those "elided" views: `_day.html.erb`, `_event.html.erb`, `day_timeline/columns/*`, `days/index.html.erb`, `event/_layout.html.erb`, and `index.html.erb`. These are the building blocks. I'll be looking for how event data is structured, iterated through, and ultimately presented. I'll pay attention to any helper methods or partials being used to ensure a grasp of all the different contexts. I expect to find things like event titles, descriptions, dates, times, and any associated visual elements. Given my experience, I'll be looking for any hints of optimization – perhaps lazy loading, caching, or other performance considerations.

Then, I'll shift gears slightly to the "card" aspect. It seems the system uses a card-based UI as well. I'll need to figure out how these "cards" relate to or interact with events. I see a comprehensive listing of views: `cards/display/mini/_meta.html.erb`, `cards/display/perma/_meta.html.erb`, `cards/display/preview/_bubble.html.erb`, `cards/container/*`, `cards/show.html.erb`, `public/boards/**/*`. This indicates different card representations (mini, perma, preview), potentially within containers, with a public-facing aspect. I'll read through these views, paying close attention to any inheritance or overriding that is happening between the views to see how these different cards are constructed. I'll want to trace how card data is retrieved, formatted, and ultimately rendered across different contexts (show pages, boards, previews, etc.). The * and *** wildcards should encompass subdirectories or more comprehensive sets. I need to see how these different views compose and what logic controls when each is used. The `public` directory is critical – I'll need to understand any client-side rendering or API interactions, and how the data is being exposed to the user.

Finally, I'll be looking for consistency. Are events and cards presented in a similar way, or are there distinct approaches? Are there any common components, templates, or helpers that are used across both? My goal is a complete understanding of the event and card rendering pipeline from data retrieval to final presentation.

**Comprehensive Date and Time Inventory & Analysis**

Okay, I've got a complete inventory of every place in this codebase where dates and times are rendered. Now, let's break this down.

Firstly, the key is to move *all* date/time rendering to the browser. The server only needs to send raw timestamps. The goal is to provide a consistent, user-specific display, addressing page caching issues and handling diverse timezones gracefully. This is essential for a smooth user experience.

Here's the detailed rundown, keeping in mind caching and potential timezone leaks:

1.  **`app/views/cards/comments/_comment.html.erb`**: This uses `strftime` directly, and it's *cached*. The current format is `"%A, %B %-d", comment.created_at.strftime("%l:%M %p").strip`. This needs conversion to the user's timezone on the client, and we have to be *very* careful with the cache keys.
2.  **`app/views/cards/display/common/_meta.html.erb`, `app/views/cards/display/preview/_meta.html.erb`, and `app/views/cards/display/public_preview/_meta.html.erb`**: These use `time_ago_in_words` and are all cached. That `time_ago_in_words` is *definitely* suspect and needs attention. This requires local-time conversion.
3.  **`app/views/cards/display/common/_stamp.html.erb`**: This is cached and has server-rendered `strftime` dates in the `bridge_description` attribute and `strong` tag! This screams "timezone leak." Also, the `MutationObserver` in `bridge/stamp_controller.js` is triggered by client-side updates (probably `data-bridge-description`), which means *we're* updating this div! This requires careful attention.
4.  **`app/views/cards/container/_closure.html.erb`**: This uses `strftime` for closed dates and `time_ago_in_words` for relative dates. This requires local-time conversion. The `time_ago_in_words` needs to be addressed and replaced with a browser-rendered alternative, particularly concerning future dates.
5.  **`app/views/notifications/notification/_header.html.erb`**: Also *cached* with `strftime`. It's essential to convert the notification's date and time to the user's timezone in the client.
6.  **`app/views/my/access_tokens/_access_token.html.erb`**: Uses `strftime`. Need to update rendering to client-side.
7.  **`app/views/events/_empty_days.html.erb`**: `strftime` is used, and it could be impacted by the "text-transform: capitalize" CSS on the HTML! We must ensure that relative days are correctly capitalized. The use of `beginning_of_day` timestamps is also worth reviewing in relation to timezones.
8.  **`app/views/events/day_timeline/_column.html.erb` and `app/models/user/day_timeline/column.rb`**: This combines a server-rendered date title (`strftime`) with a time-only display (`strftime`) with cached events! And then it uses `TimeHelper`! We need *careful* testing and refactoring here. `Time.zone.name` is in the cache key.
9.  **`app/views/searches/_result.html.erb`**: `strftime`. To be updated to the user's timezone.
10. **`app/views/webhooks/_delivery.html.erb`**:  `strftime` and `time_ago_in_words`. To be updated to the user's timezone.
11. **`app/helpers/bridge_helper.rb`**:  `bridge_share_card_description` calls `strftime` for date formatting, this needs to be moved to the client.
12. **`app/views/sessions/magic_links/show.html.erb`**: Includes `distance_of_time_in_words`, but it deals with a static duration, not a timestamp. Server-rendered, no change necessary.
13. **JSON Views**: These are already sending UTC timestamps, so they're fine. API responses shouldn't be touched.
14. **Other Considerations**: I need to cross-check:
    *   *SaaS Views*: Ensure they're also addressed, but not before checking `AGENTS.md`.
    *   *Email Templates*:  Email templates MUST be rendered server-side.

**Analyzing Time Formatting with Stimulus Controllers**

Okay, here's the deal. I was just looking at the layout files, `application.html.erb` and `public.html.erb`, and noticed something interesting in the `<body>` tags: a bunch of Stimulus controllers are already being applied. It got me thinking, why not add a `local-time` controller there, too?  I mean, we already have all those other controllers, `timezone-cookie`, `turbo-navigation`, etc. Why not leverage that setup?  This could be done in BOTH layout files!  And it just hit me:  `app/javascript/controllers/local_time_controller.js` would fit right in!

So, the idea is to manage local time formatting using Stimulus, and I see two clear approaches, which I really need to analyze carefully:

*   **Pattern 1**: A single `local-time` controller on the `<body>`. We'd use Stimulus targets like `time`, `date`, `datetime`, and `ago`, and then attach those to any HTML `<time>` element. The controller would handle the periodic refresh using `setInterval` (or other method) and update all those targets accordingly.
*   **Pattern 2**: Put a `local-time` controller directly on each individual `<time>` element, or, an alternative could be a Web Component `<local-time>`, or even still using `<body>` but with targets.

Now, let's really break down the pros and cons of these patterns. Let's compare Pattern 1 (the single controller on `<body>`) versus Pattern 2 (a controller on each `<time>` element).

**Performance Considerations**

Imagine a scenario:  Let's say we have a board with 100 cards, and each card has two `<time>` tags, that's 200 time elements, and also comments, notifications, etc. This is where the performance implications start to be noticeable.

*   **Pattern 1 (Single Controller)**:
    *   Only *one* instance of the controller.
    *   *One* `setInterval` call to refresh all those time values.  (Or, better yet, `requestAnimationFrame` for efficiency.)
    *   *One* set of cached `Intl.DateTimeFormat` formatters – way less overhead.
    *   Stimulus will automatically trigger the related `TargetConnected` function when a `<time>` element is added to the DOM, whether it's through the initial page load, Turbo Frame loads, Turbo Stream appends/replaces/morphs, or other dynamic insertions.
*   **Pattern 2 (Multiple Controllers)**: A distinct Stimulus controller for each time element, with associated overhead.

**Turbo Morph Considerations**

Wait a second. What happens when we use Turbo Morph?  Let's consider this specific case: The server sends `<time data-local-time-target="ago" datetime="2025-01-20T12:00:00Z"></time>`, and the existing DOM has `<time data-local-time-target="ago" datetime="2025-01-20T12:00:00Z">5 days ago</time>`.

*   **Morph's Behavior**: When using `morphdom` or `idiomorph`, the server's HTML has empty text (or fallback text) inside the `<time>`. If the existing `<time>` element has text like "5 days ago," the morph operation *replaces* the content with an empty string!
*   **Stimulus and `targetConnected`**: The critical part is that since the `<time>` element is morphed, Stimulus won't trigger `targetConnected` or `connect()` again.
*   **Solution**: To get around this, we need to listen for the `turbo:morph@window` event (or `turbo:morph-element@document`, `turbo:before-morph-element` or `turbo:render`). I just saw in `app/views/events/index/filter/_board.html.erb` that the application has events to handle Turbo morphs, so we should check how they work!!  Also `app/views/cards/show.html.erb` / `layouts/shared/_head.html.erb` uses `<% turbo_refreshes_with method: :morph, scroll: :preserve %>`, and we need to check the tests for this functionality.

This is a really important detail!  I need to check how Fizzy handles Turbo morphing to handle the local time formatting properly. We should look at `test/system/card_refresh_test.rb` and grep the whole repo for "turbo:morph" to learn how we are managing these changes.

steps.reasoning_content:
**Analysis of Timezone Handling and Proposed Solution**

Okay, here's my understanding of this situation. We're tasked with moving time rendering to the client-side for better caching and a more accurate user experience across timezones. I've been carefully reviewing the existing codebase and the task description.

Initially, I was concerned about the existing `date_helpers.js` and its use of the `<meta name="timezone">` tag, along with the `Time.zone.name` on the server. The comment in `date_helpers.js` about matching "client day boundaries with the server's" seemed counterintuitive to the goal of rendering times in the *browser's* timezone. Why would we care about server-side day boundaries if we're moving time rendering to the client?

My analysis led me to the conclusion that if we *do not* change `date_helpers.js`, we can achieve our goals.

The issue stems from how the application previously handled time. The server was rendering times in its own timezone (UTC by default before the timezone cookie is set). The `<meta name="timezone">` tag was likely introduced to ensure that any client-side calculations (like those done in `date_helpers.js` and `bubble_controller.js`) would align with the server's time, *even if the client didn't have a timezone cookie* (or when a cached page was used!). This approach created a problem: times were baked into the HTML in the server's timezone, which isn't what we want.

The task specifies that all time rendering must move to the browser. *That means that we must use the browser's own timezone (standard JS `Intl.DateTimeFormat` / `Date` local timezone), not the server's timezone.* This is critical for achieving the correct display of times in the user's local timezone.

Now, concerning `date_helpers.js`. Its purpose was to make calculations of day differences, which is important for `bubble_controller.js`, and its code makes calculations based on `beginningOfDay`, and `signedDifferenceInDays`. It was built that way because, originally, the repo rendered times on the server, and because of this, the client-side functions needed to agree with the server's.

Here's why `date_helpers.js` is *not* a problem *if* we're rendering times on the client:

*   The comment says to snap to midnight to have consistent day boundaries with the server. If we render times locally, there is no need to make the calculations consistent.
*   By using the browser's timezone (`new Date()`, `getFullYear()`, `getMonth()`, `getDate()`, `Date.UTC(...)`), we are correctly accounting for the user's timezone when determining time differences. There is no need to modify `date_helpers.js`.

In the end, as long as we make *all* time rendering (formatting, display) fully client-side using the browser's timezone, we can leave `date_helpers.js` alone, and *that* would be the correct solution.

I'm immediately thinking about a specific pitfall with `Intl.DateTimeFormat`. I need to revisit the infamous "gotcha" with `Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-US", { hour: "numeric", minute: "2-digit" })`. I know that in newer ICU versions, Node versions, and Chrome versions, there can be a subtle but significant issue.

Specifically, in Chrome (and presumably Chromium-based systems) from version 72 onwards, formatting a date using this method can sometimes insert a narrow no-break space (`\u202f`) or even a regular space (` `) between the time (like "1:42") and the AM/PM indicator. Now, the real question is: Does `\u202f` break string matching of a basic string like `"1:42 PM"`?

This is a critical catch! Let's check what Chromium's output actually is within this particular container! Immediately, I'm thinking about running a quick test directly. class Event::Description
  include ActionView::Helpers::TagHelper
  include ERB::Util

  attr_reader :event, :user

  def initialize(event, user)
    @event = event
    @user = user
  end

  def to_html
    to_sentence(creator_tag, card_title_tag).html_safe
  end

  def to_plain_text
    to_sentence(creator_name, quoted(card.title)).html_safe
  end

  private
    def to_sentence(creator, card_title)
      if event.action.comment_created?
        comment_sentence(creator, card_title)
      else
        action_sentence(creator, card_title)
      end
    end

    def creator_tag
      tag.span data: { creator_id: event.creator.id } do
        tag.span("You", data: { only_visible_to_you: true }) +
        tag.span(event.creator.name, data: { only_visible_to_others: true })
      end
    end

    def card_title_tag
      tag.span card.title, class: "txt-underline"
    end

    def creator_name
      h event.creator.name
    end

    def quoted(text)
      h %("#{text}")
    end

    def card
      @card ||= event.action.comment_created? ? event.eventable.card : event.eventable
    end

    def comment_sentence(creator, card_title)
      "#{creator} commented on #{card_title}"
    end

    def action_sentence(creator, card_title)
      case event.action
      when "card_assigned"
        assigned_sentence(creator, card_title)
      when "card_unassigned"
        unassigned_sentence(creator, card_title)
      when "card_published"
        "#{creator} added #{card_title}"
      when "card_closed"
        %(#{creator} moved #{card_title} to "Done")
      when "card_reopened"
        "#{creator} reopened #{card_title}"
      when "card_postponed"
        %(#{creator} moved #{card_title} to "Not Now")
      when "card_auto_postponed"
        %(#{card_title} moved to "Not Now" due to inactivity)
      when "card_resumed"
        "#{creator} resumed #{card_title}"
      when "card_title_changed"
        renamed_sentence(creator, card_title)
      when "card_board_changed", "card_collection_changed"
        moved_sentence(creator, card_title)
      when "card_triaged"
        triaged_sentence(creator, card_title)
      when "card_sent_back_to_triage"
        %(#{creator} moved #{card_title} back to "Maybe?")
      end
    end

    def assigned_sentence(creator, card_title)
      if event.assignees.include?(user)
        "#{creator} will handle #{card_title}"
      else
        "#{creator} assigned #{assignee_names} to #{card_title}"
      end
    end

    def unassigned_sentence(creator, card_title)
      "#{creator} unassigned #{unassigned_names} from #{card_title}"
    end

    def renamed_sentence(creator, card_title)
      %(#{creator} renamed #{card_title} (was: "#{old_title}"))

    end

    def unassigned_names
      h(event.assignees.include?(user) ? "yourself" : assignee_names)

    def old_title

    end

    def new_location

    end

    def column

First, I need to revisit `app/javascript/helpers/date_helpers.js`. It's used by `bubble_controller.js` and therefore, directly impacts how the bubble timelines are rendered. This file specifically says it deals with timezone issues, which is exactly what we are trying to fix! The code attempts to snap a timestamp to midnight using the server's timezone via the `<meta name="timezone" content="UTC">` tag. The code talks about "client day boundaries match the server's instead of following the browser's resolved timezone, which can differ in a PWA". Okay, I get it now. This file attempts to handle potential discrepancies between the server's timezone and the browser's, especially in PWAs. So, the question is, why is the `date_helpers.js` *not* using the timezone cookie? It looks like previously, there were issues in iOS PWAs where `Intl.DateTimeFormat().resolvedOptions().timeZone` sometimes diverged from the server's `Time.zone`, affecting day timelines. I need to make sure this code is still correct, especially since a test might be run with a timezone override. The browser will take the time zone of the browser. So, on the first visit to the application, we'd be in good shape. Because the browser will take the timezone of the device. Okay, it doesn't break anything. And, the `bubble_controller.js` is fine.

Second, a deep dive is required into the caching implications. The critical question: If we move time rendering to the browser, will it invalidate our cached fragments? I need to analyze how time is rendered *within* those fragments. Let's look at a few common fragments.

Okay, here's my thought process on the test plan, as I see it:

**Testing Strategy for Timezone Handling**

Right, let's nail this down. We need to be absolutely thorough. My initial plan is to systematically approach testing timezone handling in this application, covering multiple layers and ensuring robust coverage. I'm thinking:

1.  **Helper Methods:** First, I'll need to test the core time helper methods themselves. This means creating `test/helpers/time_helper_test.rb`. We'll need to confirm they are accurate, that they handle various date and time formats correctly, and deal with all the edge cases. Then there will be the need to verify the bridge methods in `test/helpers/bridge_helper_test.rb`.

2.  **Controller Integration:** Then I'll focus on the rendering process within the controllers. `test/controllers/local_time_rendering_test.rb` will be crucial. I'll need to check every single HTML endpoint to ensure the timezones are rendering correctly. And critically, I need to verify *cacheability* across timezones. We don't want timezone information leaking between users!

3.  **End-to-End System Tests:** Lastly, and this is where it gets really important, I have to cover the whole user experience. This means real Chromium-based system tests, found in `test/system/local_time_test.rb`. Here I'll verify the handling across different timezones, checking the full rendering process. I'll need to test morphing, streams, all different views, and the tricky JS edge cases. This is where we'll confirm that the user sees the time as expected, regardless of how they access it.

Let's start by creating the helper tests and the controller tests, and run those. We need to build up the foundation.

require "test_helper"

class TimeHelperTest < ActionView::TestCase
  test "local_datetime_tag renders empty time element with UTC ISO-8601 datetime" do
    timestamp = Time.utc(2025, 9, 12, 20, 42, 0)

    html = local_datetime_tag(timestamp, style: :daysago)

    assert_equal %(<time datetime="2025-09-12T20:42:00Z" class="local-time-value" data-local-time-target="daysago"></time>), html
  end

  test "local_datetime_tag defaults to time style" do
    timestamp = Time.utc(2025, 9, 12, 20, 42, 0)

    html = local_datetime_tag(timestamp)

    assert_equal %(<time datetime="2025-09-12T20:42:00Z" class="local-time-value" data-local-time-target="time"></time>), html
  end

  test "local_datetime_tag emits identical HTML regardless of server timezone" do
    timestamp = Time.utc(2025, 9, 12, 20, 42, 0)

    ny_html = Time.use_zone("America/New_York") { local_datetime_tag(timestamp.in_time_zone, style: :daysago) }
    tokyo_html = Time.use_zone("Asia/Tokyo") { local_datetime_tag(timestamp.in_time_zone, style: :daysago) }
    utc_html = Time.use_zone("UTC") { local_datetime_tag(timestamp.in_time_zone, style: :daysago) }

    assert_equal utc_html, ny_html
    assert_equal utc_html, tokyo_html
  end

  test "local_datetime_tag merges custom classes and data attributes" do
    timestamp = Time.utc(2025, 9, 12, 20, 42, 0)

    html = local_datetime_tag(timestamp, style: :date, class: "custom-time", data: { test: "value" })

    assert_includes html, %(class="local-time-value custom-time")
    assert_includes html, %(data-test="value")
    assert_includes html, %(data-local-time-target="date")
    assert_includes html, %(datetime="2025-09-12T20:42:00Z")
  end

  test "local_datetime_tag handles Date objects" do
    date = Date.new(2025, 9, 12)

    html = local_datetime_tag(date, style: :date)

    assert_equal %(<time datetime="2025-09-12" class="local-time-value" data-local-time-target="date"></time>), html
  end

  test "local_datetime_tag returns nil for blank datetime" do
    assert_nil local_datetime_tag(nil)
    assert_nil local_datetime_tag("")
  end
end
EOF

class LocalTimeRenderingTest < ActionDispatch::IntegrationTest
  setup do
    sign_in_as :kevin
  end

  test "card show renders raw UTC timestamps for meta, comments, and auto-close notice" do
    card = cards(:logo)
    comment = comments(:logo_agreement_kevin)

    get card_path(card)
    assert_response :success

    assert_select "body[data-controller~='local-time']"
    assert_select ".card__meta-text--added time.local-time-value[datetime='#{card.created_at.utc.iso8601}'][data-local-time-target='daysago']", text: ""
    assert_select ".card__meta-text--updated time.local-time-value[datetime='#{card.last_active_at.utc.iso8601}'][data-local-time-target='daysago']", text: ""
    assert_select "##{dom_id(comment)} .comment__permalink-title time.local-time-value[datetime='#{comment.created_at.utc.iso8601}'][data-local-time-target='daysago']", text: ""

    assert_select "##{dom_id(card, :closure_notice)}" do |elements|
      assert_no_match(/\bin\s+<time/, elements.first.to_html)
      assert_select "time.local-time-value[datetime='#{card.entropy.auto_clean_at.utc.iso8601}'][data-local-time-target='indays']", text: ""
    end
  end

  test "closed card renders raw UTC timestamps for stamp, bridge description, and closure message" do
    card = cards(:shipping)
    assert card.closed?

    get card_path(card)
    assert_response :success

    iso = card.closed_at.utc.iso8601
    assert_select ".card__closed[data-local-time-target='date'][data-local-time-attribute='data-bridge-description'][data-datetime='#{iso}']"
    assert_select ".card__closed[data-bridge-description]", count: 0
    assert_select ".card__closed-date time.local-time-value[datetime='#{iso}'][data-local-time-target='date']", text: ""
    assert_select ".card-perma__closure-message time.local-time-value[datetime='#{iso}'][data-local-time-target='shortdate']", text: ""
  end

  test "cached card and comment HTML is identical across viewer timezones" do
    card = cards(:logo)
    comment = comments(:logo_agreement_kevin)

    cookies[:timezone] = "America/Los_Angeles"
    get card_path(card)
    assert_response :success
    la_card_html = css_select("##{dom_id(card, :card_container)}").to_html

    assert_equal la_comment_html, tokyo_comment_html
    assert_equal css_select("##{dom_id(card, :meta)}").to_html, Nokogiri::HTML::DocumentFragment.parse(la_card_html).css("##{dom_id(card, :meta)}").to_html

  end

    assert_select "td time.local-time-value[datetime='#{token.created_at.utc.iso8601}'][data-local-time-target='datetime']", text: ""

steps.reasoning_content:
Okay, here's my take on those test issues.

**Test Bug Dissection**

Right, let's see... those three pesky little test failures. Turns out they're all pretty straightforward:

1.  That `BridgeHelperTest`… the root is that the `ERB::Util` module is being directly included. Either that, or, as a more indirect way to include it, is being automatically included when a class includes `ActionView::TestCase`, which has the `h` method defined in `ERB::Util`.
2.  The `LocalTimeRenderingTest` is comparing the `css_select` results directly, which is problematic. It's not re-parsing with `Nokogiri::HTML::DocumentFragment.parse`, so the HTML escaping issue is rearing its ugly head. The comparison needs to be done on re-parsed data.
3.  The issue with the fixture name for the access token is probably just a typo. I'll take a look at `test/fixtures/identity/access_tokens.yml` and see what's what.

Okay, now to go fix those and re-run. Simple.

require "application_system_test_case"

class LocalTimeTest < ApplicationSystemTestCase
  include ActionView::RecordIdentifier

  setup do
    sign_in_as(users(:david))
  end

  teardown do
    set_browser_timezone("")
  end

  test "comments render relative times and clock times in the viewer timezone" do
    tz = timezone_in_midday
    set_browser_timezone(tz)

    zone = ActiveSupport::TimeZone[tz]
    now = Time.current.in_time_zone(zone)

    card = cards(:layout)
    card.comments.destroy_all

    two_hours_ago = (now - 2.hours).change(min: 42, sec: 0)
    last_night = (now - 1.day).change(hour: 23, min: 15, sec: 0)
    five_days_ago = (now - 5.days).change(hour: 12, min: 0, sec: 0)
    older_same_year = if now.yday > 15
      (now - 14.days).change(hour: 12, min: 0, sec: 0)
    else
      nil
    end
    last_year = zone.local(now.year - 1, 9, 12, 13, 42, 0)

    c_today = card.comments.create!(creator: users(:kevin), body: "Two hours ago", created_at: two_hours_ago)
    c_yesterday = card.comments.create!(creator: users(:kevin), body: "Last night", created_at: last_night)
    c_five_days = card.comments.create!(creator: users(:kevin), body: "Five days ago", created_at: five_days_ago)
    c_older = older_same_year && card.comments.create!(creator: users(:kevin), body: "Older this year", created_at: older_same_year)
    c_last_year = card.comments.create!(creator: users(:kevin), body: "Last year", created_at: last_year)

    visit card_url(card)

    expected_clock = two_hours_ago.strftime("%-l:%M %p")
    assert_equal expected_clock, comment_time_text(c_today)
    assert_includes comment_time_title(c_today), expected_clock

    assert_equal "yesterday", comment_time_text(c_yesterday)
    assert_equal "5 days ago", comment_time_text(c_five_days)

    if c_older
      assert_equal older_same_year.strftime("%b %-d"), comment_time_text(c_older)
    end

    assert_equal "Sep 12, #{now.year - 1}", comment_time_text(c_last_year)
  end

  test "same cached HTML renders in each viewer's own timezone" do
    card = cards(:layout)
    card.comments.destroy_all

    # Pick a timestamp 30 minutes ago so it is guaranteed in the past; LA and Tokyo differ by 16-17 hours
    timestamp = (Time.current - 30.minutes).change(sec: 0)
    comment = card.comments.create!(creator: users(:kevin), body: "Cross-timezone comment", created_at: timestamp)

    with_actionview_partial_caching do
      set_browser_timezone("America/Los_Angeles")
      visit card_url(card)
      la_text = comment_time_text(comment)
      la_expected = expected_daysago_in_zone(timestamp, "America/Los_Angeles")
      assert_equal la_expected, la_text

      set_browser_timezone("Asia/Tokyo")
      visit card_url(card)
      tokyo_text = comment_time_text(comment)
      tokyo_expected = expected_daysago_in_zone(timestamp, "Asia/Tokyo")
      assert_equal tokyo_expected, tokyo_text

      assert_not_equal la_text, tokyo_text
    end
  end

  test "card auto-close notice reads today, tomorrow, and in N days in viewer timezone" do
    tz = timezone_in_midday
    set_browser_timezone(tz)

    zone = ActiveSupport::TimeZone[tz]
    now = Time.current.in_time_zone(zone)

    card = cards(:logo)
    period = card.entropy.auto_clean_period

    # Auto-closing overnight (tomorrow morning in viewer timezone)
    tomorrow_morning = (now + 1.day).change(hour: 2, min: 0, sec: 0)
    card.update_column(:last_active_at, tomorrow_morning - period)
    visit card_url(card)
    assert_selector "##{dom_id(card, :closure_notice)}", text: "Moves to “Not Now” tomorrow if there’s no activity."

    # Auto-closing in 3 days
    in_three_days = (now + 3.days).change(hour: 12, min: 0, sec: 0)
    card.update_column(:last_active_at, in_three_days - period)
    visit card_url(card)
    assert_selector "##{dom_id(card, :closure_notice)}", text: "Moves to “Not Now” in 3 days if there’s no activity."

    # Auto-closing later today
    later_today = (now + 1.hour).change(sec: 0)
    card.update_column(:last_active_at, later_today - period)
    visit card_url(card)
    assert_selector "##{dom_id(card, :closure_notice)}", text: "Moves to “Not Now” today if there’s no activity."
  end

  test "closed card stamp, bridge description, and completion message render in viewer timezone" do
    card = cards(:shipping)
    # 2025-09-13 02:00:00 UTC is Sep 12 in America/Los_Angeles and Sep 13 in Asia/Tokyo
    card.closure.update!(created_at: Time.utc(2025, 9, 13, 2, 0, 0))

    set_browser_timezone("America/Los_Angeles")
    visit card_url(card)

    assert_equal "Sep 12, 2025", find_time_text(".card__closed-date time")
    assert_equal "Sep 12, 2025", find(".card__closed")["data-bridge-description"]
    assert_selector ".card-perma__closure-message", text: /Completed by .+ on Sep 12, 2025\./

    set_browser_timezone("Asia/Tokyo")
    visit card_url(card)

    assert_equal "Sep 13, 2025", find_time_text(".card__closed-date time")
    assert_equal "Sep 13, 2025", find(".card__closed")["data-bridge-description"]
    assert_selector ".card-perma__closure-message", text: /Completed by .+ on Sep 13, 2025\./
  end

  test "public card renders times in browser timezone" do
    board = boards(:writebook)
    board.publish
    card = cards(:logo)
    card.update_columns(created_at: Time.utc(2024, 9, 12, 20, 42, 0), last_active_at: Time.utc(2024, 9, 12, 20, 42, 0))

    set_browser_timezone("America/Los_Angeles")
    visit published_card_url(card)

    assert_equal "Sep 12, 2024", find_time_text(".card__meta-text--added time")
    assert_equal "Sep 12, 2024", find_time_text(".card__meta-text--updated time")
  end

  test "broadcast morph preserves rendered local times" do
    set_browser_timezone("America/Los_Angeles")
    Current.user = users(:kevin)
    card = cards(:layout)
    card.update_columns(created_at: Time.utc(2024, 9, 12, 20, 42, 0))

    visit card_url(card)
    assert_equal "Sep 12, 2024", find_time_text(".card__meta-text--added time")

    assert_selector "turbo-cable-stream-source[connected]", visible: :all
    assert_no_selector "turbo-cable-stream-source:not([connected])", visible: :all

    card.update!(title: "Morphed title check")
    perform_enqueued_jobs only: Turbo::Streams::BroadcastStreamJob

    assert_selector "h1", text: "Morphed title check", wait: 5
    assert_equal "Sep 12, 2024", find_time_text(".card__meta-text--added time")
    assert_not_equal "", find_time_text(".card__meta-text--updated time")
  end

  test "posting a new comment renders its local time immediately via Turbo Stream" do
    set_browser_timezone("America/Los_Angeles")
    card = cards(:layout)

    visit card_url(card)
    fill_in_lexxy with: "Freshly posted comment"
    click_on "Post"

    assert_text "Freshly posted comment"
    comment = card.comments.order(:created_at).last
    assert_match(/\A\d{1,2}:\d{2} [AP]M\z/, comment_time_text(comment))
  end

  test "events timeline, notifications, access tokens, and webhooks render times in browser timezone" do
    set_browser_timezone("America/Los_Angeles")

    # Access tokens
    token = identities(:david).access_tokens.create!(description: "TZ check", permission: "read", created_at: Time.utc(2025, 9, 12, 20, 42, 0))
    visit my_access_tokens_url
    assert_equal "9/12/25, 1:42 PM", find_time_text("time[datetime='#{token.created_at.utc.iso8601}']")

    # Webhooks
    webhook = webhooks(:active)
    delivery = webhook_deliveries(:successfully_completed)
    delivery.update_column(:created_at, Time.utc(2024, 9, 12, 20, 42, 0))
    visit board_webhook_url(webhook.board, webhook)
    assert_equal "Sep 12, 2024", find_time_text("##{dom_id(delivery)} time")

    # Notifications
    notification = notifications(:logo_mentioned_david)
    notification.update_column(:created_at, Time.utc(2024, 9, 12, 20, 42, 0))
    visit notifications_url
    assert_equal "Sep 12, 2024", find_time_text("##{dom_id(notification)} .card__timestamp time")

    # Events timeline
    event = events(:layout_assignment_jz)
    event.update_column(:created_at, Time.current.in_time_zone("America/Los_Angeles").change(hour: 13, min: 42, sec: 0))
    visit events_url
    assert_selector ".events__column-header time", text: /\A(today|yesterday|[A-Z][a-z]+, [A-Z][a-z]+ \d{1,2})\z/i
    assert_match(/\A\d{1,2}:\d{2} [AP]M\z/, find_time_text(".event__timestamp time"))
  end

  test "local_time_helpers handles DST, year boundaries, leap years, and invalid inputs" do
    visit card_url(cards(:logo))

    set_browser_timezone("America/New_York")
    results = page.evaluate_async_script(<<~JS)
      const done = arguments[arguments.length - 1];
      import("helpers/local_time_helpers").then((h) => {
        const ref = new Date("2025-09-12T19:42:00Z"); // 3:42 PM EDT
        const dstSpringNow = new Date("2025-03-10T04:30:00Z"); // Mar 10 00:30 EDT
        const dstSpringBefore = new Date("2025-03-09T04:30:00Z"); // Mar 8 23:30 EST (24h earlier, 2 calendar days!)
        const newYearsDay = new Date("2026-01-01T14:00:00Z"); // Jan 1 2026 9:00 AM EST
        const newYearsEve = new Date("2026-01-01T03:00:00Z"); // Dec 31 2025 10:00 PM EST
        const dec27 = new Date("2025-12-27T17:00:00Z"); // Dec 27 2025 12:00 PM EST (5 days before Jan 1)
        const dec20 = new Date("2025-12-20T17:00:00Z"); // Dec 20 2025 (12 days before Jan 1, prior year)
        const leapDay = new Date("2024-02-29T17:00:00Z");
        const marchFirst = new Date("2024-03-01T17:00:00Z");

        done({
          sameDay: h.formatDaysAgo(new Date("2025-09-12T17:42:00Z"), ref),
          yesterday: h.formatDaysAgo(new Date("2025-09-12T02:00:00Z"), ref), // Sep 11 10:00 PM EDT
          fiveDaysAgo: h.formatDaysAgo(new Date("2025-09-07T17:00:00Z"), ref),
          sixDaysAgo: h.formatDaysAgo(new Date("2025-09-06T17:00:00Z"), ref),
          sevenDaysAgo: h.formatDaysAgo(new Date("2025-09-05T17:00:00Z"), ref),
          priorYear: h.formatDaysAgo(new Date("2024-09-12T17:42:00Z"), ref),
          inDaysOverdue: h.formatInDays(new Date("2025-09-10T17:00:00Z"), ref),
          inDaysToday: h.formatInDays(new Date("2025-09-12T22:00:00Z"), ref),
          inDaysTomorrow: h.formatInDays(new Date("2025-09-13T06:00:00Z"), ref), // Sep 13 2:00 AM EDT
          inDaysThree: h.formatInDays(new Date("2025-09-15T17:00:00Z"), ref),
          inDaysThirty: h.formatInDays(new Date("2025-10-12T17:00:00Z"), ref),
          agoDayToday: h.formatAgoDay(ref, ref),
          agoDayYesterday: h.formatAgoDay(new Date("2025-09-11T17:00:00Z"), ref),
          agoDayEarlier: h.formatAgoDay(new Date("2025-09-05T17:00:00Z"), ref),
          agoDayPriorYear: h.formatAgoDay(new Date("2024-09-12T17:00:00Z"), ref),
          dstSpringDiff: h.differenceInCalendarDays(dstSpringBefore, dstSpringNow),
          newYearsYesterday: h.formatDaysAgo(newYearsEve, newYearsDay),
          newYearsFiveDays: h.formatDaysAgo(dec27, newYearsDay),
          newYearsPriorYearDate: h.formatDaysAgo(dec20, newYearsDay),
          leapYesterday: h.formatDaysAgo(leapDay, marchFirst),
          dateOnlyParsed: h.formatDate(h.parseDate("2025-09-12")),
          invalidDate: h.parseDate("not-a-date"),
          blankDate: h.parseDate("")
        });
      });
    JS

    assert_equal "1:42 PM", results["sameDay"]
    assert_equal "yesterday", results["yesterday"]
    assert_equal "5 days ago", results["fiveDaysAgo"]
    assert_equal "6 days ago", results["sixDaysAgo"]
    assert_equal "Sep 5", results["sevenDaysAgo"]
    assert_equal "Sep 12, 2024", results["priorYear"]
    assert_equal "today", results["inDaysOverdue"]
    assert_equal "today", results["inDaysToday"]
    assert_equal "tomorrow", results["inDaysTomorrow"]
    assert_equal "in 3 days", results["inDaysThree"]
    assert_equal "in 30 days", results["inDaysThirty"]
    assert_equal "today", results["agoDayToday"]
    assert_equal "yesterday", results["agoDayYesterday"]
    assert_equal "Friday, September 5", results["agoDayEarlier"]
    assert_equal "Thursday, September 12, 2024", results["agoDayPriorYear"]
    assert_equal 2, results["dstSpringDiff"]
    assert_equal "yesterday", results["newYearsYesterday"]
    assert_equal "5 days ago", results["newYearsFiveDays"]
    assert_equal "Dec 20, 2025", results["newYearsPriorYearDate"]
    assert_equal "yesterday", results["leapYesterday"]
    assert_equal "Sep 12, 2025", results["dateOnlyParsed"]
    assert_nil results["invalidDate"]
    assert_nil results["blankDate"]
  end

  private
    def set_browser_timezone(timezone_id)
      page.driver.browser.execute_cdp("Emulation.setTimezoneOverride", timezoneId: timezone_id)
    end

    # Choose an IANA timezone where local hour is comfortably midday (04:00..19:59)
    # so 2 hours ago is always today and 1 hour from now is always today.
    def timezone_in_midday
      %w[ UTC America/New_York America/Los_Angeles Asia/Tokyo Pacific/Auckland ].find do |tz|
        hour = Time.current.in_time_zone(tz).hour
        hour >= 4 && hour <= 19
      end || "UTC"
    end

    def comment_time_text(comment)
      find_time_text("##{dom_id(comment)} .comment__permalink-title time")
    end

    def comment_time_title(comment)
      find("##{dom_id(comment)} .comment__permalink-title time")[:title]
    end

    def find_time_text(selector)
      element = find(selector)
      # Read textContent so CSS text-transform (capitalize/uppercase) doesn't alter exact DOM text
      page.evaluate_script("arguments[0].textContent", element)
    end

    def expected_daysago_in_zone(timestamp, tz)
      zone = ActiveSupport::TimeZone[tz]
      local_time = timestamp.in_time_zone(zone)
      local_now = Time.current.in_time_zone(zone)
      diff_days = (local_time.to_date - local_now.to_date).to_i

      if diff_days == 0
        local_time.strftime("%-l:%M %p")
      elsif diff_days == -1
        "yesterday"
      else
        "#{diff_days.abs} days ago"
      end
    end
end
